metaData.originalTitle: Codex 更新远程控制，你也终于可以在手机上随时随地 Vibe Coding 了。
metaData.title: Codex Remote Control Update: Now You Can Vibe Code Anywhere on Your Phone
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI has launched a remote control feature for Codex, allowing users to remotely control Codex running on their home computer via ChatGPT on their phone, enabling a space-unrestricted Vibe Coding experience.
metaData.summary: This article introduces OpenAI's new remote control feature for Codex, which allows users to remotely connect to and control Codex running on their home computer through the ChatGPT app on their phone. The author details the setup process: enabling mobile settings in Codex on the computer, generating a QR code, scanning it with the phone to authorize login, and achieving real-time synchronization between the phone and computer. Once connected, the phone can send new tasks, view worker threads, check outputs, approve commands, and more. All files, credentials, and permissions remain on the local computer, with communication secured by a relay layer. The author compares this experience with Claude Code's remote control, finding Codex to have fewer bugs and a smoother experience, and shares a real-world case of modifying a project while traveling. The article also outlines other recent important updates to Codex, including Computer Use (background computer control), a built-in browser (supporting direct annotations and comments), a Chrome extension (leveraging logged-in browser state to interact with websites), and integration with gpt-image-2 for generating images directly within code. The author believes the competition between Codex and Claude Code mirrors the golden age of iOS vs. Android and recommends using both to adapt to changes.

mainPoints.point: Codex launches remote control, enabling phone-based programming on a desktop computer.
mainPoints.explanation: Users can remotely connect to Codex on their home computer via the ChatGPT app on their phone, enabling a space-unrestricted Vibe Coding experience with a simple setup process, real-time synchronization, and task management.

mainPoints.point: Codex's remote control experience is superior to Claude Code's, with fewer bugs.
mainPoints.explanation: The author finds Codex's remote control experience smoother, noting that Claude Code often suffers from bugs like selector rendering errors, while Codex's synchronization and operations are more stable and reliable.

mainPoints.point: Codex has been updated frequently, with its feature completeness continuously improving.
mainPoints.explanation: Beyond remote control, Codex has also introduced features like Computer Use, a built-in browser, a Chrome extension, and in-code image generation. Paired with GPT-5.5, it has received positive feedback and its usage share is approaching that of Claude Code.

keyQuotes: You can use ChatGPT on your phone to directly remote control Codex on your home computer, enabling a vibe coding experience without space limitations.
Your phone message is just a router sending messages to Codex on your home computer.
The back-and-forth pace between Codex and Claude Code honestly reminds me of the golden age when iOS and Android were copying each other's homework.
I think you need to use both of these products. That way, no matter how the wind blows, you won't be left behind.
